items.title: Face poset and order complex
items.statement: The face poset consists of nonempty faces ordered by inclusion. For a poset P, its order complex has vertices P and finite totally ordered subsets as faces, including the empty face.
items.proof_route: Check closure under subsets; distinguish the empty poset from a poset with a least element.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.source_locator: 2.5.10, pp.51–52 (face-chain description); general-poset formulation is an explicit abstraction of the face-chain construction, not a quotation

items.title: Barycentric subdivision of an abstract simplicial complex
items.statement: sd K is the order complex of the nonempty face poset of K; sd of a subcomplex is a subcomplex.
items.proof_route: Singleton faces become vertices; no vertex is assigned to the empty face.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Canonical barycentric realization map
items.statement: b_K sends vertex sigma to |sigma|^{-1} times the sum of its vertices, and extends affinely on chains.
items.proof_route: Every chain lies in its maximal face, so the affine extension lies in |K|; empty realizations give the empty map.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Finite simplicial weak topology agrees with euclidean topology
items.statement: For finite K, the weak topology is the Euclidean subspace topology in R^{V(K)}; in particular it is compact metric and Hausdorff. Every finite subcomplex P of arbitrary K embeds as a closed subspace |P| of |K|, with this same topology.
items.proof_route: A weakly closed subset is the finite union of its closed intersections with the compact Euclidean simplices, each closed in the ambient space. The converse follows by restriction. This replaces the invalid union-of-open-extensions argument in the published proposition, without modifying that item. For the embedding clause, a closed subset of |P| is a finite union of closed subsets of its simplices; each has closed intersection with every simplex of K. Conversely every ambient closed set restricts to a closed set on |P|.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Barycentric face chains triangulate a geometric simplex
items.statement: The barycenters of each strict face chain are affinely independent, and their simplices triangulate the original simplex, with precisely common-chain-face intersections.
items.proof_route: Induct over dimension: triangulate the boundary compatibly and cone from the interior barycenter. Every ray from the barycenter meets the boundary once; this gives coverage and intersections. Alternatively order coordinate levels and recover positive weights uniquely; ties omit zero-weight vertices.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Barycentric subdivision realizes homeomorphically
items.statement: For every abstract K with weak realization topology, b_K:|sd K| -> |K| is a homeomorphism, compatible with all subcomplex inclusions.
items.proof_route: The finite-simplex homeomorphisms agree on common faces. Continuity of b_K and its inverse follows by restricting to each original simplex and each subdivided simplex, using weak topology. Never invoke a global finite-union argument for infinite K.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Open and closed stars in a subdivision
items.statement: The open vertex star consists of points with positive coordinate at that vertex; the closed star is the subcomplex of faces of simplices containing it. Apply this separately to K and sd K.
items.proof_route: The open star is weakly open by restriction to each simplex; identify its closure simplexwise. A collection only of cofaces is not itself a subcomplex.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Compact subsets of an arbitrary simplicial realization meet finitely many open simplices
items.statement: Assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice, every compact subset of |K| meets finitely many open simplices and is contained in a finite subcomplex, with no local-finiteness assumption. In particular a finite family of continuous maps from compact simplices has image in one finite subcomplex.
items.proof_route: If infinitely many interiors meet C, choose countably many distinct interiors and one point from each. Every subset of the chosen set meets every closed simplex finitely and is therefore weakly closed. The chosen set is a closed discrete compact space, a contradiction. Add finitely many faces. This selection uses countable choice available in ZFC; do not claim a choice-free proof.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: An augmented simplicial cone has an explicit chain contraction
items.statement: Here K is a cone with apex a precisely when sigma union {a} is a face for every face sigma of K. If K is a simplicial cone with specified apex a, its augmented integral complex contracts by h[v0,...,vn]=[a,v0,...,vn], with repeated vertices interpreted as zero and h[-1](1)=[a].
items.proof_route: Repeat the alternating-boundary computation for a cone, not merely a full simplex; d h+h d=id, including degree -1. In particular sd of a full simplex is a cone with apex its maximal face.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.source_locator: 2.1, p.121, cone identity adapted to oriented simplicial chains

items.title: Simplicial chain maps carried by specified cones are chain homotopic
items.statement: Let each simplex sigma of K be assigned a cone subcomplex Phi(sigma) of L with specified contraction, nested under faces. Any two augmentation-preserving chain maps carried by Phi are joined by a carried chain homotopy.
items.proof_route: Set h[-1]=0; recursively h(sigma)=c_Phi(sigma)(f(sigma)-g(sigma)-h(d sigma)). The bracket is a cycle by the induction identity and d squared=0; apply the specified contraction. No unproved general acyclic-carrier theorem is invoked.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.source_locator: 4.3.9 proof, p.119, carried induction; specialized cone version

items.title: Oriented simplicial subdivision operator
items.statement: The graded subdivision operator S:C_n(K;Z)->C_n(sd K;Z) sends each oriented simplex to its consistently oriented top-dimensional subdivided simplices, S_0[v]=[{v}].
items.proof_route: Define orientation via the affine realization and give the equivalent recursive formula S(sigma)=c_sigma S(d sigma) on augmented chains with S[-1]=id. Name it a graded operator until boundary compatibility is proved.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Oriented simplicial subdivision commutes with boundary
items.statement: dS=Sd on the augmented complex, hence also on ordinary chains.
items.proof_route: Cone recursion gives d c S d=S d-c d S d=S d by induction. Explain that this is precisely cancellation of internal codimension-one faces; check dimensions zero and one.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Last vertex map is carried by original simplices
items.statement: For a specified total order on V(K), lambda:sd K->K sends a nonempty face to its greatest vertex. It is simplicial and carried by original faces.
items.proof_route: Nested faces have selected vertices in the largest face. For finite K the order is a finite choice; for arbitrary K existence of such an order is supplied by ZFC, or retain the order as data.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Simplicial subdivision is a chain map and homology isomorphism
items.statement: For an abstract simplicial complex equipped with a chosen total order on its vertices, S is a chain-homotopy equivalence on integral ordinary and augmented chains. Its inverse up to homotopy is lambda_#. Consequently subdivision preserves ordinary homology and the local augmented reduced convention, including degree -1.
items.proof_route: For lambda S and id use carrier the full original simplex. For S lambda and id on a face chain use carrier sd of its largest face, a cone; deleting the maximum only shrinks the carrier. Apply carried induction to both composites. The inverse homology map is independent of chosen order. Tensoring these explicit identities gives any abelian coefficients only after the coefficient complex is explicitly defined.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Mesh of iterated simplicial barycentric subdivision tends to zero
items.statement: If finite Euclidean K has dimension n>=1, simplex mesh(sd^r K)<= (n/(n+1))^r mesh(K); every vertex star has diameter at most twice simplex mesh. Empty and zero-dimensional complexes have mesh zero.
items.proof_route: For nested nonempty faces F<G, b_G=(|F|/|G|)b_F+(1-|F|/|G|)b_{G\F}; bound their distance by n/(n+1) times the diameter of the original simplex. Diameter of a convex hull equals the maximum vertex distance. Distinguish simplex mesh from Maunder star-cover mesh.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: The open star criterion produces a simplicial map
items.statement: For finite K, continuous f:|K|->|L| and vertices g(v) with f(st(v)) subset st(g(v)), g extends simplicially. f(x) and |g|(x) lie in the carrier simplex of f(x); straight-line interpolation is continuous, fixed where they agree, and respects every given subcomplex pair mapped by f.
items.proof_route: The empty source is immediate. Fix a finite vertex enumeration of K and enumerate its rational barycentric grids by increasing denominator and lexicographic order, with repetitions; rounding coordinates in each simplex proves this sequence d_j dense. The image C=f(|K|) is compact: pull back any open cover and use compactness of |K|. If the union of supports of f(d_j) were infinite, recursively take the least j whose image support is not contained in the finite union of previously selected supports. The resulting distinct points q_n meet each closed target simplex tau in at most |vertices(tau)| points: each such occurrence adds a fresh vertex of tau. Every subset of {q_n} therefore meets every simplex in a finite closed set, so is weakly closed. Thus {q_n} is closed in C and discrete, contradicting compactness via its singleton cover. The union W of supports is consequently finite. The subcomplex P of all target simplices with vertices in W is finite and weakly closed (its intersection with each simplex is a finite union of faces). The closed set f^{-1}(|P|) contains the dense sequence, hence equals |K|. No Countable Choice is used: all infinitely repeated selections were least natural indices. For each source simplex use its barycenter in the star criterion to show the images of its vertices span a target face. For arbitrary x, each positive-coordinate vertex v has g(v) in the carrier of f(x), so |g|(x) and f(x) lie in that same simplex of P. Finite weak and Euclidean subspace topologies agree; H(x,t)=(1-t)f(x)+t|g|(x) is continuous into |P| and then |L|. It fixes every point where the maps agree and remains in each specified target subcomplex on the corresponding source subcomplex.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.source_locator: 2C.1 and 2C.2 proofs, pp.178–179; Appendix A.1, p.520, closed-discrete argument. The finite-source rational-grid/least-index choice-free refinement is proved locally, not attributed to Hatcher.

items.title: Finite simplicial approximation for maps of pairs
items.statement: For finite K, A subset K and B subset L, every continuous f:(|K|,|A|)->(|L|,|B|) has a simplicial approximation g:(sd^r K,sd^r A)->(L,B) for all sufficiently large r, homotopic as a map of pairs to f b_K^r.
items.proof_route: Pull back target open stars; choose 2 mesh < the Lebesgue number. Finite vertex choices give g. The carrier argument keeps A in B throughout. This does not fix a positive-dimensional simplicial restriction pointwise.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Relative derived subdivision of a finite simplicial pair
items.statement: For finite A subset K define D_A K by leaving A unchanged and, in increasing dimension, coning each subdivided boundary of a simplex outside A from its barycenter. Iterate with A fixed.
items.proof_route: Prove this is a linear subdivision by the same radial cone argument; D_empty K=sd K. Each original subcomplex receives a compatible subdivision.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Relative derived subdivision makes the fixed subcomplex full
items.statement: After one relative derived subdivision A is full: each simplex meets |A| in a face or the empty set; later relative derived subdivisions preserve this.
items.proof_route: List simplices as a face of A followed by a strict chain of larger faces outside A. The vertices lying in A span exactly that face. Include A empty and A=K.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Relative subdivision neighbourhood adjustment
items.statement: For finite A subset K, a further subdivision near A admits a piecewise affine h:|K|->|K| homotopic to id rel |A|, sending a neighbourhood of A into A. Off that neighbourhood the remaining vertex stars shrink under sufficiently many relative subdivisions; near A their h-images are subordinate to vertex stars of A.
items.proof_route: Use Maunder 2.5.20 construction K+ between D_A K and D_A^2 K: move barycenters of mixed simplices to an A-vertex in their A-face, leaving A and the supplement fixed. Fullness makes this simplicial and keeps the homotopy in original faces. Track inherited stars under further subdivisions using vertex selection. Proposition 2.5.19 provides shrinkage only away from the fixed region.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Relative simplicial approximation after subdivision
items.statement: Let K,L be finite complexes, A subset K, and f:|K|->|L| continuous with f|A simplicial. For some r there is g:D_A^r K->L with |g|=f on |A| and |g| homotopic to f rel |A|. Thus it is a homotopy of pairs (K,A)->(L,f(A)). A preassigned compatible linear subdivision on A can be extended before applying this assertion.
items.proof_route: Approximate f h, not f itself. Away from A use shrinking stars and a finite Lebesgue number; near A use the neighbourhood adjustment and simplicial restriction. Set g(v)=f(v) on A, and concatenate the two homotopies. Extension of a subdivision on A is the same boundary-coning induction defining relative subdivision. Never promise an ordinary iterated barycentric source subdivision fixed on a nonconstant edge.

references.title: E. C. Zeeman, Relative simplicial approximation (1964)

items.source_locator: Theorem and proof, pp.39–42; Maunder 2.5.20 pp.55–56

items.title: Finite convex cell complex and linear subdivision
items.statement: A finite convex cell complex in Euclidean space consists of compact convex polyhedral cells, includes their faces and the empty cell, and intersections are common faces. A linear subdivision has the same underlying set and every new simplex is contained in an old cell.
items.proof_route: Use finite systems of affine inequalities for the intersection cells; explicitly define faces by active supporting equalities. Do not confuse these finite convex cells with arbitrary CW cells.

references.title: C. P. Rourke and B. J. Sanderson, Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology

items.source_locator: Chapter 2, Cells and Cell Complexes, pp.13–15

items.title: Intersections of finite linear complexes form a convex cell complex
items.statement: If two finite linear simplicial complexes have the same underlying polyhedron, their nonempty intersections, with all faces, form a finite convex cell complex refining both. Each cell has finitely many faces and a relative interior point; its proper faces cover its boundary.
items.proof_route: Write each simplex by barycentric nonnegativity in its affine hull; combine finite inequalities. Active constraints define the finite face lattice. A point with all non-identically-zero inequalities strict is obtained by averaging finite witnesses. Use maximal line segments to prove boundary coverage. Check that intersections of intersection cells are faces of each by adding active constraints.

references.title: C. P. Rourke and B. J. Sanderson, Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology

items.title: Finite convex cell complexes admit compatible triangulations
items.statement: Any finite convex cell complex has a simplicial triangulation obtained by choosing one relative interior point in each nonempty cell and coning its already triangulated boundary in increasing dimension.
items.proof_route: Dimension zero starts the induction. The ray from the chosen point to any other point meets the boundary exactly once; cones cover and have common-face intersections. Use common boundary triangulations for adjacent cells.

references.title: C. P. Rourke and B. J. Sanderson, Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology

items.title: Two finite linear subdivisions have a common simplicial refinement
items.statement: Two finite linear subdivisions of a fixed finite Euclidean simplicial complex have a common finite simplicial refinement.
items.proof_route: Intersect the two finite families of cells and triangulate that intersection complex compatibly. The underlying set is unchanged and containment in both original triangulations is immediate. This makes no assertion about arbitrary homeomorphic triangulations or common stellar subdivisions.

references.title: C. P. Rourke and B. J. Sanderson, Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology

title: Simplicial Subdivision and Simplicial Approximation: Examples

items.title: Barycentric subdivision of an edge and triangle
items.statement: An edge subdivides into two edges; a triangle into six triangles indexed by maximal nonempty face chains.
items.proof_route: List chains vertex<edge and vertex<edge<triangle. Check face and empty-complex counts.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: The subdivision chain of an oriented two simplex
items.statement: Compute S[a,b,c] and its boundary explicitly, preserving orientation.
items.proof_route: Expand the six oriented triangles from the apex-first cone recursion. Compute their boundaries: three barycenter-to-edge-center edges cancel first, and the three barycenter-to-original-vertex edges cancel in the remaining sum, leaving exactly the subdivided original boundary.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: A relative simplicial approximation fixed on the endpoints
items.statement: For f:[0,1]->[0,1], f(x)=x^2, a simplicial map after midpoint subdivision can be homotopic to f rel both endpoints.
items.proof_route: Send vertices 0,1/2,1 to 0,0,1. The affine realization g stays in the target edge; (1-t)x^2+t g(x) fixes 0 and 1.

references.title: E. C. Zeeman, Relative simplicial approximation (1964)

items.title: A compact set in an infinite non locally finite realization still meets finitely many cells
items.statement: In the weak realization of countably many edges sharing a vertex, any compact subset lies in finitely many edges, although the common vertex is not locally finite.
items.proof_route: Display the two-segment compact subset and calculate its four support faces. Display the points at parameter 1/n on distinct edges and prove their set closed discrete. For arbitrary compact C, each coordinate has an attained supremum by the finite-subcover argument; its positive maximum determines a unique point on that edge. If infinitely many coordinates were active these canonical points would be closed discrete in C, contradicting compactness. This specialized proof needs no Countable Choice; the general compact-support lemma is mentioned only with its explicit hypothesis.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: A continuous map need not be simplicial before subdivision
items.statement: A continuous self-map of an edge can fail to be simplicial in the original triangulation.
items.proof_route: f(x)=x^2 fixes both vertices, whereas the unique simplicial self-map fixing them is x. At x=1/2 the values differ. This is a failure of exact simpliciality, not a claim that f has no simplicial approximation.

references.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Ordinary barycentric subdivision cannot fix a nonconstant simplicial edge
items.statement: If the fixed subcomplex contains an edge mapped identically to an unsubdivided target edge, a simplicial map from sd^r K to that target cannot agree pointwise there for r>=1.
items.proof_route: Its source midpoint is a vertex and would have to map to the target midpoint, which is not a vertex. Relative derived subdivision avoids this obstruction.

references.title: E. C. Zeeman, Relative simplicial approximation (1964)
